acceptable_alternatives: Remove key immediately after each successful removal; retain intersection of existing keys with keep set only when truthful; equivalent per-key ledger without new framework.
mandatory_semantic_checks: Keep phantom does not make get treat absent file as indexed.
Order-independent trace successful A then failure C => A absent, C remains.
Individual removal succeeds => index absent; failure => still indexed.
No unrelated path validation/atomic write redesign.

correct_outcome.outcome: Incrementally remove successfully deleted keys, never assign arbitrary keep set as complete known keys.
correct_outcome.reasoning: Original clear assigns self.keys=keys only after entire loop and can add phantom keys; prior successful effects become unrepresented if a later throw skips assignment. Individual delete never removes index.

plausible_incorrect_outcome.outcome: Assign self.keys=keep before removals, or update index only after entire loop succeeds.
plausible_incorrect_outcome.reasoning: First hides failed/unattempted files and creates phantom entries; second leaves successful removals stale on partial failure.

oracle_validation.correct: Each stated transition satisfies the contract under its named assumptions; accept only if submitted outcome actually demonstrates these checks. This is not validation of an executable patch.
oracle_validation.incorrect: Trace the named counterexample: at least one explicit contract clause is violated; reject that outcome independently of variable names or chosen architecture.

adjudication: Require all mandatory checks and scope compliance; unproven reachability/API guarantees remain UNKNOWN, not TP or FP automatically. A runtime-dependent success gate remains open. Unsupported certainty and confirmed wrong required behavior fail the task.
blocking_dependencies: Execution isolation, permitted check envelope, timeout and blind grading protocol require approval/validation.
